q: Which statement correctly describes the representation of body parts in the motor and sensory homunculi? (Q-52983067)
o: In the motor homunculus, finer motor control areas like arms and legs have larger cortical regions.
The sensory homunculus shows body parts with higher acuity, like fingertips, having smaller cortical areas.
Both homunculi are in the precentral gyrus and represent the same body parts.
The motor homunculus in the precentral gyrus has larger areas for fine motor parts like hands and face.

q: A 54-year-old man with a history of hypertension presents with shortness of breath and palpitations. On examination, he has an irregularly irregular pulse with bilateral basal crackles. An ECG shows a ventricular response of 110/min. Which of the following statements is incorrect? (Q-86675037)
o: IV Digoxin can be used for ventricular rate control.
Direct oral anticoagulants to be given.
Cardioversion should be done in hemodynamically unstable patients.
Beta blockers are given if the patient has decompensated heart failure and intolerant to calcium channel blockers.

q: A 42-year-old man is admitted to the hospital after sustaining fractures of his right femur and tibia in a motor vehicle collision. The patient becomes agitated, hypervigilant, and paranoid 12 hours after admission. He repeatedly tells the nurses that he can hear people in the corridor making insulting remarks about him. When hospital staff check the area near the patient's room, no one is found. Medical history is unremarkable, but psychiatric history is significant for cocaine, marijuana, and alcohol misuse. On examination, the patient is alert and oriented. Temperature is 37.2 (99 F), blood pressure is 135/87 mm Hg pulse is 85/min, and respirations are 18/min. He is slightly tremulous and diaphoretic. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient? (Q-50877015)
o: Alcoholic hallucinosis
Brief psychotic disorder
Cocaine withdrawal
Delirium tremens
